concept.title: Text and fonts
concept.shortdesc: The font properties of your stylesheet decide how text looks in the PDF. This chapter explains how to choose fonts, load your own and use their special features. The text and fonts reference at the end lists every property, at-rule and descriptor.

conbody.p: A font is a file that holds the shapes of the characters, called glyphs. A font family is a group of related font faces, such as the regular, bold and italic faces of one design. You choose a family with font-family, and CSSMedia picks the face that best matches the weight, width and style that you request.
CSSMedia gets fonts from three places:

ul.li: The 14 standard fonts of PDF: Times, Helvetica, Courier, Symbol and ZapfDingbats. They are built in.
The fonts in the folder that you pass with the -f option.
The fonts that your stylesheet declares with @font-face.

conbody.p: CSSMedia does not read the fonts installed in your computer, so a PDF looks the same on every computer. It embeds the fonts that it loads in the PDF.
